Observed assistant message snapshots; provider estimates, not invoice

external_invariants: Model: GPT2LMHeadModel with n_layer=12, n_embd=768, n_head=12, vocab_size=50257, n_positions=1024, resid_pdrop=embd_pdrop=attn_pdrop=0.0, use_cache=False, attn_implementation='eager', FP32, train mode, initialized immediately after torch.manual_seed(20261020).

Data: per-rank synthetic token IDs drawn with torch.Generator().manual_seed(31000 + rank); accumulation_steps=4 tensors of shape (micro_batch=1, sequence_length=128) with values in [0, 50257); no other dataset exists (request assets are empty by design).

Numerics: FP32 end to end; torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=False; torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32=False; torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=False; torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest'); no autocast, no GradScaler, no compilation.

Accumulation: optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) at step start; loss for each micro-batch is model(input_ids=tokens, labels=tokens, use_cache=False).loss / 4; first 3 micro-batches run under DDP no_sync, only the final micro-batch triggers gradient synchronization; reported loss is the sum of the 4 scaled micro losses and must be finite.

Optimizer: SGD(lr=0.001, momentum=0.0, weight_decay=0.0, foreach=False); exactly one optimizer.step() per workload repetition; SGD keeps no momentum state so the reset only reloads the initial weights.

DDP configuration: broadcast_buffers=False, bucket_cap_mb=25, gradient_as_bucket_view=True, device_ids=[bound device index]; find_unused_parameters stays False; no communication hooks are registered in the measured path (the source registers its inventory hook only in a separate diagnostic step).

Cross-rank semantics: after the final micro-batch every rank holds bitwise-identical gradients (source exact_gradient_replica_check with atol=0, rtol=0); effective global batch = world_size 2 x micro_batch 1 x accumulation_steps 4 = 8 micro-batches = 1024 tokens per step.
Reset fidelity: every repetition starts from the same initial weights (CPU state_dict snapshot), empty gradients, empty optimizer state and the prepare-time RNG states.

Timing hygiene: control coordination (barrier, peak-memory reset, synchronization) uses the separate gloo group and happens outside the timer; the only NCCL collectives in the measured workload are the DDP gradient allreduces of the final accumulation micro-batch; step_ms must stay <= 1.05x baseline.

Observations: loss, per-micro losses, every gradient tensor and every updated parameter of the ~124M-parameter model are exposed as full tensors; no elapsed times or performance counters appear in observations.
Quality scope: gradient/parameter comparisons use atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-4 (request.quality); reference fidelity only, no downstream accuracy or convergence claim.

Workload frozen: batch, sequence_length=128, accumulation_steps=4, world_size=2, architecture, FP32 precision, seeded data, completion boundary and quality checks are never altered to improve a score.

selection.rationale: The measured step's only communication is the DDP gradient allreduce of the final accumulation micro-batch: 13 NCCL RING_LL calls (12x28.35MB buckets produced by the 25MB cap, plus the 157.5MB embedding bucket) moving 497.76MB per rank. This selected group is the dominant member: the twelve 28.35MB bucket allreduces carry 206.4ms of the 264.2ms diagnostic CUDA total. Independently collected nsys diagnostics show NCCL kernels busy 62.2ms on the earlier rank with only ~9.6ms overlapped by backward compute (~52.6ms exposed), while the peer rank waits inside NCCL kernels (197.1ms skew-inflated kernel sum); the clean step_ms baseline is 142ms, so exposed allreduce time is the largest addressable component of the project metric. The 28.35MB payloads run on the latency-oriented LL protocol at ~8.4GB/s and pay launch/rank-meet overhead thirteen times per step. Bucket boundaries are fixed by DDP(bucket_cap_mb=25) at model-wrap time in gpt2_ddp_training.py:59, a single editable code boundary whose reducer launches exactly this group's calls (d0938de87369efd500322679); note that any bucket reconfiguration necessarily reshapes the sibling embedding-bucket call b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b (group 8525af72c631b94e3dd0), so the eventual edit must be validated for the whole allreduce phase even though this selection owns the twelve-bucket group. The workload, accumulation/no_sync structure, optimizer, completion boundary, FP32/TF32 policy and quality checks stay frozen; for a 2-rank elementwise SUM, per-element results are invariant to bucket boundaries, so cross-rank bitwise-identical gradients and the reference-tolerance checks are preserved.
selection.hypothesis: Consolidating the gradient buckets (raising bucket_cap_mb so the twelve 28.35MB layer buckets of this group form a few large contiguous allreduces instead of twelve latency-bound LL calls) reduces per-call NCCL launch and rank-meet overhead, lets NCCL pick a higher-bandwidth protocol/geometry for large contiguous payloads, and collapses per-bucket skew stalls, thereby shrinking exposed communication and step_ms below the 142ms baseline while also lowering max_rank_nccl_kernel_sum_ms. Expected benefit is a hypothesis to be tested, not a guarantee: if transfers stay LL-bound near 8.4GB/s only the per-call and skew overhead (~10-20ms) is recovered, and coarser buckets reduce overlap granularity; paired measurement against the clean baseline must confirm the improvement within the 1.05x step constraint and all numeric checks.

proposal.rationale: Selected group f833b57a373d8262a384 is the twelve per-bucket c10d.allreduce_ calls (d0938de87369efd500322679) that the DDP reducer issues for the 28.35 MB FP32 layer buckets (bucket_cap_mb=25) during the final, gradient-synchronizing micro-batch. Target-resources show them as twelve separate ncclDevKernel_AllReduce_Sum_f32_RING_LL launches: 40.5 ms CUDA on rank 0 and 206.4 ms skew-inflated on rank 1, so per-call launch/rank-meet overhead and per-bucket skew stalls dominate the addressable communication. DDP construction is frozen inside prepare (bucket_cap_mb fixed at wrap time), so the bucket layout itself cannot be edited; instead the replacement implements the selection's consolidation hypothesis at the operator boundary. The callable is installed identically on both ranks. Calls 1..N-1 (N=12 from the observed per-rank count) stash their single bucket tensor and return an already-completed genuine c10d Work token; call N issues ONE c10d.allreduce_ on the full twelve-tensor list through the parent operator. ProcessGroupNCCL executes a multi-tensor allreduce inside a single nccl group: one large contiguous collective (340 MB) that reduces every bucket in place, letting NCCL drop the latency-oriented LL protocol for a high-bandwidth geometry and collapsing thirteen per-step rank-meet points for this group into one. The grouped call's real Work is returned for call N, so the DDP reducer's existing finalize-time wait retains exactly the baseline synchronization barrier before optimizer.step() consumes the gradients; no CPU-side blocking is added, and the small compute/communication overlap the baseline had (~9.6 ms) is traded for a single much cheaper collective. Correctness: for the 2-rank elementwise SUM every element remains one addition of the two rank values regardless of bucket boundaries, so per-element results, in-place bucket/grad aliasing (gradient_as_bucket_view=True), and cross-rank replica identity are preserved; the sibling embedding-bucket call b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b (group 8525af72c631b94e3dd0) has a different tensor signature, is routed by the framework's signature guard to the unmodified operator, and both ranks issue the grouped call before the embedding call, so per-communicator NCCL ordering keeps collective sequences matched across ranks. No calls are eliminated: all twelve op sites still execute through the replacement (coverage counts 12 per run per rank), and the cohort state resets every twelve calls, matching the plan for controls, quality, warmup and measured repetitions alike. Expected effect on the frozen metrics is a reduction of exposed communication and step_ms below the 142 ms baseline with a lower diagnostic.max_rank_nccl_kernel_sum_ms (13 kernels per step become 2: one grouped 340 MB kernel plus the untouched 157.5 MB embedding kernel); this is the selection's hypothesis to be confirmed by paired GPU measurement, not an assumed fact. No previous-feedback.txt was supplied, so this is the first attempt with no prior worker feedback to incorporate. No tunable parameters are declared: cohort size 12 (single grouped launch) minimizes rank-meet points, and any smaller cohort would only re-introduce per-group stalls without restoring meaningful overlap, so a parameter sweep would add risk without a plausible mechanism for improvement.

setup_work.build_time: No allocations, no parameter or state transforms, no changes to model, DDP wrapper or optimizer at build time; build only reads the observed spec (cohort count) and the parent operator reference.
setup_work.first_invocation: During the first quality invocation only, the replacement lazily allocates one 4-byte zero FP32 tensor on the bound device and issues one 4-byte async allreduce_ on the same NCCL process group to obtain a genuine completed c10d Work token for cohort calls 1..N-1. This happens inside quality runs, before the timed measure repetitions.
setup_work.steady_state: No extra collectives: each step's calls 1..11 return the previous cohort's completed grouped Work as the token, and call 12 performs exactly one twelve-tensor grouped allreduce_ through the parent operator. The workload executes fully on every invocation; nothing fixture-dependent is cached.
setup_work.synchronization: The grouped Work returned at call 12 is waited by the DDP reducer at finalize, exactly like the baseline per-bucket Works; calls 1..11 return already-completed Works, which is sound because gradient consumption begins only after the reducer has waited every bucket's Work. No new CPU blocking, streams, barriers or CUDA graphs are introduced.
setup_work.memory: Retained for the process lifetime: one 4-byte device tensor, the stashed bucket tensor references within an open cohort (DDP bucket buffers that are already resident), and two Work objects. No staging buffer, no weight packing, no CUDA Graph pools. Peak allocated/reserved impact is below allocator granularity (a single 512-byte block at most); framework lifecycle peaks should be unchanged.

quality_risks: Protocol/geometry change: the grouped call replaces twelve RING_LL kernels with one large grouped collective. For the 2-rank elementwise SUM each element is still a single addition of the two rank values, so gradients are expected to stay bitwise-identical across ranks and within the 1e-6/1e-4 reference tolerances, but this must be confirmed by the paired GPU validation.

Deferred Work tokens: calls 1..11 return an already-completed Work while their buckets are actually reduced by the cohort-final grouped Work. Correctness relies on the DDP reducer waiting every per-bucket Work at finalize before gradients are consumed (the baseline barrier). The tokens are genuine c10d Work objects produced by the same NCCL process group, so wait()/completion/exception queries behave exactly like baseline Works.

Cohort alignment assumes the observed plan (exactly twelve matching calls per run per rank, issued in identical topological order on both ranks, embedding-bucket call excluded by signature). If a run deviated, the stash would mis-align; guards forward any structurally unexpected call to the parent, and the plan is fixed by the frozen workload.

Performance risk, not quality: if the interconnect keeps the 340 MB transfer near the LL effective rate, only per-call launch and skew overhead is recovered, and the ~9.6 ms of baseline compute/communication overlap is forfeited; step_ms must still satisfy the 1.05x baseline constraint, which paired measurement verifies.
First-cohort seeding adds one 4-byte allreduce to the very first quality run only; steady-state measured runs and NCCL-kernel diagnostics contain no additional collectives.
